neighbours.label: certainty / guarantee phrasing: 'to be sure', 'the only way to be sure', 'always possible' - the point where the text asserts something is guaranteed
fire: Weigh the parcel again at the counter if you want to be sure the postage is right.
Testing every batch in the lab is the only way to be sure the water is clean.
With a full backup it is always possible to restore the server to last night's state.
Count the tickets twice so that you can be sure nobody was left off the list.
Since the matrix is symmetric, it is always possible to choose an orthogonal basis.
Ask the pharmacist directly; that is the only way to be sure the two drugs are safe together.
Call the venue the day before to be sure the room is still reserved for us.
Whatever the input size, it is always possible to finish the sort in a bounded number of passes.
quiet: Weigh the parcel again at the counter if you suspect the postage is wrong.
Testing every batch in the lab is one of several steps that keep the water clean.
With a partial backup it is sometimes hard to restore the server to last night's state.
Count the tickets twice because somebody was probably left off the list.
Since the matrix is not symmetric, it may be hard to choose an orthogonal basis.
Ask the pharmacist directly; she might know whether the two drugs are safe together.
Call the venue the day before in case the room is no longer reserved for us.
Depending on the input size, the sort may or may not finish in a bounded number of passes.

notes: Card: peaks on ' make', ' be', ' sure', ' only', ' always' in 'the only way to', 'to be sure', 'is always possible'; the output direction promotes ' guaranteed', ' guarantees', ' ensures', ' regardless'. Probes were uneven: 'to be sure' 0.47 and 'always possible' 0.23, but 'the only way to protect' 0.07 and 'make sure' 0.01. The test leans on the two that fired; near misses hedge the same statements.
